claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has an as-reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed machine-learning model can incorporate explicit hierarchical-microstructure descriptors alongside composition and processing features.
Relevant descriptors include local order parameters and spatial composition variance.
Hierarchical-heterostructure and local-chemical-fluctuation descriptors mediate the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Adding explicit microstructural information physically constrains the machine-learning model.
The proposed framework can capture elastic behavior, including Young's modulus.
The proposed framework can capture fracture behavior and fracture toughness.
Using the proposed model will reduce the need for computationally expensive simulations.
Ab initio and molecular-dynamics calculations are time-consuming and difficult to apply in high-throughput alloy screening.
CALPHAD can require significant computing resources and can be limited by incomplete high-entropy-alloy databases.
The relevant state-of-the-art baseline methods do not incorporate explicit hierarchical-microstructure descriptors.
The model will predict the yield strength and fracture toughness of HfNbTiVAl10 at least 15% more accurately than the stated baseline.
The model will predict Young's modulus more accurately than the stated baseline.
The model will reduce computational expense by 20–30% relative to CALPHAD and high-fidelity first-principles methods.
Predictions remain valid under standardized tensile and fracture tests when samples retain the reported hierarchical microstructure.
Processing variations or aging that alter the hierarchical microstructure may reduce model reliability.
Testing temperatures outside the calibration regime may reduce model reliability.
Machine-learning models are sensitive to training-set coverage and may be only interpolative.
Blind tensile and fracture-toughness testing of identically processed samples in multiple independent laboratories can prospectively evaluate the model.
The precise accuracy and cost improvements are uncertain because the relation between the proposed descriptors and macroscopic properties is not fully mapped across testing regimes.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires at least a 15% improvement in accuracy relative to baseline, whereas the falsification rule refers to predictions deviating by more than 15% 'in accuracy.' A prediction error threshold is not equivalent to a relative improvement threshold, so the rule does not directly test the stated accuracy claim.
